# Scientific Calculator

> A free scientific calculator that works offline: fractions, trigonometry, logarithms, formulas and constants, a unit converter, a graph, a solver, statistics, matrices and complex numbers, and a history of past calculations, exported as text or CSV. Nothing leaves your browser.

A static web app (no account, no server, no tracking): everything is calculated in the browser. Installable as an app on iOS, Android and desktop. Also available as a Chrome extension.

## Links
- [Calculator](https://raad.dev/calculator/): the app, with options and a guide to every function
- [For schools and organizations](https://raad.dev/calculator/admin): turning features of the Chrome extension off for students, from the Google Admin Console
- [Source code and documentation](https://github.com/raad-altaie/scientific-calculator): README, tests, MIT license

## Facts
- Precision: about 15 significant digits (IEEE 754 doubles), shown to 13.
- Angle units: degrees, radians, gradians. Fraction mode. Fix, Sci and Eng formats.
- Panels: formulas and constants; unit converter, with days between dates and dates moved on; graph (functions, sliders, roots and crossings, areas, derivatives, equations and inequalities of x and y, polar and parametric curves, recursive and explicit sequences, best fits); solver (roots of equations in exact form as well, inequalities, turning points, polynomials, linear systems, two curves, integrals, sums to infinity, limits, Taylor series, areas between curves, arc lengths, differential equations, time value of money (N, I/Y, PV, PMT, FV), NPV, IRR and payback, loan payment schedules, APR and APY, normal, t, chi-squared, F, binomial, Poisson, geometric, hypergeometric, exponential and uniform distributions, confidence intervals); statistics (mean, median, quartiles, standard deviation, variance, mode, histogram and box plot; pairs with their line of best fit and correlation); numbers (matrices up to 10 × 10 with eigenvalues, powers, row reduction, null space, LU and QR, least squares; vectors; complex numbers and polynomials of them; bases and bits, any base from 2 to 36, text and Unicode codes, IEEE 754; prime factors, GCD and LCM, modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, exact big numbers, primes, fractions and repeating decimals).
- Author: Raad Altaie. License: MIT.
